sections.title: Summary
sections.content:
The salsa step in house dance is a groovy forward-and-back foot pattern built on the signature house bounce. The dancer keeps a steady, relaxed rhythm, letting the knees soften and the body pulse gently with the beat.

The movement alternates between a light forward tap and a light backward tap, each done without committing weight, creating a playful, syncopated feel.

sections.title: Basic step
sections.content: Start in a relaxed parallel stance. Tap the right foot forward on the first count without dropping the heel, then replace it. Tap the left foot back on the next count. Keep the bounce in the knees and the chest quiet.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.content:
• Dumping weight onto the tapping foot so the bounce dies.
  • Making the step large instead of keeping it under the body.

sections.title: Musicality
sections.content: Ride the kick and the hi-hat. The salsa step is a groove, not a travel step — stay in place and let the bounce mark the bar.

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: The house bounce is a small, continuous pulse through the knees and hips. Everything else in house sits on top of it.

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: The cross body lead takes the follower across the lead's line while keeping the slot clear and the connection light.

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: A freeze stops the body on the beat in a controlled pose. Strength and lines matter more than how long you can hold it.

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Jack in the box is a compact house footwork phrase that drops and pops back up without losing the bounce.

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Cuban motion comes from bending and straightening the knees so the hips settle naturally, not from swinging the waist.
